findings.freeAreaFinding: Practical know-how articles tended to explain concrete value before the paid boundary rather than relying on paid-area length.

note.decision: Treat 1,480-1,980 JPY as a test band for sufficiently strong practical know-how articles, but do not reprice existing articles until product-level sales/PV data exist. New practical articles may enter this band when their promised outcome and evidence support it.

BOOTH.decision: Do not discount low-ticket products merely to chase volume. Coherent bundles are attractive because the fixed 45 JPY component makes effective fee rate lower at higher order values, while the bundle must still provide genuine complementary value.

MicrosoftStore.source: Microsoft Learn Windows app performance and product page experiment documentation
findings: Acquisitions report exposes page views, install attempts, acquisitions, successful installs, first launches and conversion by source/campaign.
Custom campaign IDs can be used to attribute Store page views and conversions from external links.
Product page experiments support A/B testing of visual assets; Microsoft notes icons and screenshots can occupy up to roughly half of the product-page surface area.
Health reporting covers crashes and unresponsive events.
MicrosoftStore.decision: Before derivative Store apps or aggressive listing changes, capture the live funnel baseline. Do not start an A/B test until enough page views accumulate to avoid reacting to noise.

experiments.currentProblem: Several practical articles are priced below the 1,842 JPY average observed among note's top-20%-selling practical know-how sample, but there is no product-level conversion evidence yet.
experiments.change: For new high-value practical articles, test 1,480-1,980 JPY when the free section clearly states a concrete outcome and the paid section delivers reusable templates/workflows. Existing prices remain unchanged in this run.
experiments.expectedAOVDelta: positive if conversion remains acceptable; numeric estimate withheld until sales/PV exist
experiments.expectedLTVDelta: potentially positive through clearer entry/standard/premium role separation
experiments.requiredSample: Observed sales and PV by article across comparable themes; avoid interpreting zero/one sale as elasticity evidence.
experiments.risk: Higher price can reduce conversion if promised value is weak or audience trust is insufficient.
experiments.rollback: Return new-test articles to the prior comparable price band if conversion materially underperforms comparable articles after sufficient traffic.

experiments.currentProblem: Event Operations OS and Sponsor CRM are sold separately, leaving a coherent buyer journey without a higher-AOV bundle.
experiments.change: Prepare a genuine complementary bundle around 2,480 JPY only if both source deliverables can be legally and technically packaged together without reducing standalone value.
experiments.expectedAOVDelta: positive by construction if bundle purchases are incremental rather than cannibalizing both standalone purchases
experiments.expectedLTVDelta: positive if bundle becomes the preferred full-workflow option
experiments.requiredSample: Track bundle sales versus standalone sales after launch; no numeric forecast before observations.
experiments.risk: Cannibalization or perceived discounting of standalone products.
experiments.rollback: Keep standalone products unchanged; withdraw or reprice bundle if it shifts buyers from two-product purchases without increasing net revenue.

experiments.requiredSample: Enough page views per variant to avoid noise; no fixed threshold invented without variance/base-rate data.
